runs.note: This 1497 two-column textura is the hardest run. gemini-3.1-pro-preview has the most faithful abbreviations ('ꝯ eſt Cõciliatoris', 'ap̃a', 'p̃ternaliter'), but on p35 it transcribes ~93 lines of the facing-page sliver first. gemini-3-flash-preview is complete with no sliver text, at the cost of simplified sigla (z for ꝯ). The serious failures are flash-lite on p35, which reads only the facing-page sliver and then loops 'ꝗdē' about 2,500 times, and glm-ocr, which loops on p33 and p34 and truncates p35.

runs.note: 1521 Gothic grammar with heavy abbreviation. gemini-3.8-flash keeps the diplomatic forms (ſ, ꝛ, ⁊, macrons) with only a few slips. gemini-3-flash-preview is close but normalises spelling and expands 'pma' wrongly as 'ꝓma'. glm drops part of a line on p45 and substitutes 'cofusum' for 'q̃tum' on p46. Calamari reads the body well but turns every large display word (Sciendum, Conclusio, Arguitur) into garbage.

runs.note: 1708 Basel dissertation: title page, dedication with a braced column, and the italic opening of the Prooemium with one Greek word. runs.note: 1496 incunable of Peter of Spain, dense Gothic with heavy abbreviation. A strip of the facing leaf shows at the image edge, and both gemini-3.1-pro and the production flash-lite transcribe it as extra lines on two to three pages. Pro also truncates p688 at 'ab infer'. gemini-3.8-flash rewrites p688 into expanded classroom Latin ('secundum', 'consequentis', 'Arguitor'), which is not on the page. flash-preview stays on the page but drops most abbreviation marks on p688.
